fixes.explanation: That's how far back He goes. Jesus says, "…from the beginning of creation, ‘God made them male and female.’" (Mark 10:6). The Pharisees pointed to Moses, and He goes back before that. That's a long trip, friend, and way past last Tuesday.
I get why feeding comes to mind, since a big crowd makes you think of a hungry one. But this verse says nothing about food. It says "…He taught them, as was His custom."
That's the one. The Pharisees, a strict religious group, asked, "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?" (Mark 10:2). The verse says they came to test Him, friend.
Healing on the Sabbath is a fair guess, but this test is about marriage. In Mark 10:2 they ask, "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?" The Sabbath never comes up in that verse.

That's a paper too, but it's not the one in the verse. The Pharisees say Moses permitted a man to write his wife "…a certificate of divorce and send her away." (Mark 10:4). A deed of purchase never comes up.

Whoa, where did the elders come from? They don't show up anywhere in this exchange. Jesus gives the reason Himself: "Moses wrote this commandment for you because of your hardness of heart." (Mark 10:5). He doesn't mention anyone asking, so I'm not adding a guest to this scene.
That's a fair guess, but it isn't what Jesus says. He says "…from the beginning of creation…" (Mark 10:6). That's the very start of everything.
That's a fair guess, but Jesus doesn't stop there. He says "…from the beginning of creation…" (Mark 10:6). That's the very start of everything.
The crowds were around Him earlier in verse 1, but this happens back inside the house. Mark 10:10 says "…the disciples asked Jesus about this matter." So it's His disciples who ask.
